newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RECALLED RHODES BOOSTS SOUTH AFRICA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RECALLED RHODES BOOSTS SOUTH AFRICA.

text.p: Jonty Rhodes made a compelling return to international cricket with a brilliant 57 not out for South Africa against India in the day-night opening match of a triangular tournament at Springbok Park on Thursday.
South Africa scored 270 for four in their 50 overs as Rhodes provided a timely final flourish after half-centuries from opener Gary Kirsten (73) and Daryll Cullinan (51).

Overlooked for the three-test series against India just completed, Rhodes showed his value in the one-day game by reaching his half-century from just 35 balls and batting in all for 39 deliveries, hitting six fours.
Rhodes shared a sparkling, unbroken fifth wicket stand of 102 in 78 balls with his captain Hansie Cronje, who hit 44 not out.
Kirsten, third in the list of one-day international run scorers in 1996, emerged from a disappointing final test match to strike five boundaries in a stay of 99 balls.

He lost his opening partner Andrew Hudson to a steepling top edge for 15 and Lance Klusener, promoted to apply rapid acceleration, was unluckily run out for the same score when he tripped over trying to regain his ground.
But Cullinan continued the form that saw him make a match-saving century in the third test, putting on 111 with Kirsten for the third wicket.
Cullinan struck a six and two fours from 77 balls before being caught on the boundary in the 37th over.
Kirsten fell in the next over, cutting a short ball straight to point.
